faq.question: Can I enroll in UI/UX Design Professional as a complete beginner with no prior design experience?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum begins from foundational principles. Module 01 introduces human-centered design thinking, user discovery, and problem framing before touching software. No prior design degree, coding background, or drawing talent is required.

faq.question: Is computer programming or coding required for this course?
faq.answer: No. This is a design and visual web engineering program. Instead of writing raw HTML, CSS, or JavaScript syntax, you learn web layout principles visually in Framer (Stacks, Grids, Breakpoints) and master developer collaboration using Figma Dev Mode.

faq.question: Is Figma taught from the absolute basics?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 03 begins with canvas navigation, frames, sections, vector networks, boolean operations, and 24x24px icon craftsmanship, systematically progressing into Auto Layout v5, Component Properties, and Figma Variables in Modules 04 and 05.

faq.question: Does the course cover actual user experience (UX) research?
faq.answer: Yes. UX research is heavily emphasized in Modules 01 and 02. You learn qualitative interview protocols, Google Forms screening surveys, FigJam affinity mapping, empathy mapping, validated user personas, customer journey maps, card sorting, and user flow diagramming.

faq.question: Does the curriculum cover advanced Auto Layout and Figma Variables?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 04 is dedicated to Auto Layout v5 (Direction, Wrap, Hug/Fill/Fixed sizing, min/max dimensions, absolute positioning) and Module 05 teaches multi-tier Figma Variables (Color, Spacing, Radius, String) with instant Light and Dark mode switching.

faq.question: Will I learn responsive multi-device design?
faq.answer: Yes. You learn responsive breakpoint architecture across Desktop (1200px+), Tablet (768px/810px), and Mobile (390px) viewports in both Figma (breakpoint component variants) and Framer (native responsive media queries).

faq.question: Can students create advanced interactive prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 06 teaches high-fidelity Figma prototyping using Smart Animate physics, custom Bézier easing curves, modal overlays, sticky navbars, nested horizontal carousels, and variable-driven conditional logic (If/Else) for interactive cart and form simulation.

faq.question: Will students learn Framer in this program?
faq.answer: Yes. Framer is a core primary software platform in this course, covered extensively across 28 guided instructional hours in Module 07, plus integration in Modules 08, 09, and 10.

faq.question: Will students create and launch an actual live Framer website?
faq.answer: Yes. In Module 07 and Case Study 03, every student builds and publishes a real, production-ready, 3-page responsive marketing website deployed to a live publicly accessible `.framer.media` domain.

faq.question: Does Framer hosting require a separate paid subscription?
faq.answer: No. Framer's free plan includes full visual canvas access, 3 responsive breakpoints, CMS collections up to 10 items, and free live hosting on `.framer.media` subdomains. All required coursework runs on the free tier; paid custom domain plans are completely optional.

faq.question: Are custom domains included in the course tuition fee?
faq.answer: No. Tuition covers full instructional training and hosting on free `.framer.media` subdomains. If you choose to connect a custom top-level domain (e.g. `yourname.com`), domain registration (~$12/year) and Framer's custom domain hosting plan are paid directly to those respective vendors.

faq.question: Is Framer CMS covered in the curriculum?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 07 covers Framer CMS collection schema modeling, binding dynamic fields (rich text, images, categories, dates) to canvas layers, designing dynamic collection detail page templates, and implementing category filtering.

faq.question: Does the course teach mobile hamburger navigation in Framer?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 07 features a mandatory responsive header lab where students construct a navigation component that displays horizontal links on desktop and automatically switches to an animated mobile hamburger drawer when the browser viewport resizes.

faq.question: Does the program cover Generative AI for UX research?
faq.answer: Yes. Modules 01 and 08 teach structured prompt engineering in ChatGPT and Claude for interview discussion guide scaffolding, qualitative transcript summarization, and microcopy ideation under strict human oversight (zero fabricated research allowed).

faq.question: Does the course teach Figma AI and Figma Make?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 08 covers Figma AI features (layer auto-renaming, visual asset search, wireframe scaffolding). Figma Make component prototyping is explored, accompanied by mandatory manual component prototyping fallbacks so no student is blocked by plan tier restrictions.

faq.question: Is Framer AI and Framer Agents included?
faq.answer: Yes. Module 08 teaches the 2026 Framer Agents workflow for rapid page section scaffolding, responsive layout translation, and CMS drafting, followed by manual component refactoring to ensure accessible web standards.

faq.question: What is covered regarding the Framer Model Context Protocol (MCP) server?
faq.answer: Module 07 includes faculty-led architectural exposure to Framer's official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server released on October 22, 2026. Students learn how AI agents programmatically interact with design tokens and CMS schemas without needing to code custom servers.

faq.question: Are expensive paid AI subscriptions required?
faq.answer: No. Free tiers of ChatGPT (GPT-4o mini) and Claude are 100% sufficient for all research and copywriting exercises. Figma and Framer provide free monthly credits. Zero paid AI subscriptions are mandatory.

faq.question: Will students build comprehensive portfolio case studies?
faq.answer: Yes. Students complete 3 canonical modular assessed case studies plus 1 comprehensive Flagship Capstone: (1) Consumer Mobile App UX/UI, (2) Enterprise B2B SaaS Design System, (3) Live Framer Marketing Website with CMS, and (4) Integrated Commercial Product Launch.

faq.question: How does UI/UX Design Professional differ from Creative Design Master?
faq.answer: Creative Design Master is an 8-month multidisciplinary diploma covering 2D graphic design, InDesign packaging dielines, After Effects motion graphics, 3D animation, and basic UI. UI/UX Design Professional is a specialized 5-month program focused 100% on digital product design, advanced Figma systems, usability testing, and live web production in Framer.

faq.question: What is the tuition fee, duration, and applicable GST?
faq.answer: The selling price is flat INR 44,900 (0% artificial discount) for 5 Months (200 guided instructional hours). Statutory 18% GST (INR 8,082) is itemized on all commercial invoices, bringing the total payable fee to INR 52,982. There are zero hidden administrative charges.

faq.question: What verified career and placement assistance does Nova Skills provide?
faq.answer: Nova Skills provides 1-on-1 portfolio case study reviews, 1-page ATS product designer resume optimization, mock technical interview defense coaching, live whiteboarding challenge preparation, and direct recruitment introductions to hiring partner product teams and agencies.

faq.question: Will I own the source files and live websites I create during the course?

modules.module_title: UX Research, Problem Framing & Product Strategy
modules.module_purpose: Ground learners in evidence-based human-centered design principles, teaching them how to deconstruct ambiguous business challenges, identify genuine user pain points, formulate research hypotheses, and conduct rigorous qualitative user discovery.
what_you_will_learn: Deconstruct commercial product briefs using the Double Diamond methodology, balancing business viability with user desirability.
Design qualitative research instruments including recruitment screeners, discussion guides, and observational inquiry protocols.
Conduct ethical, unbiased 1-on-1 user interviews and deploy structured quantitative screening surveys using Google Forms.
Synthesize qualitative research in FigJam using affinity mapping, thematic clustering, and empathy mapping (Says, Thinks, Does, Feels).
Construct evidence-based user personas and customer journey maps identifying critical pain points and drop-off moments.
Leverage AI tools (ChatGPT/Claude) for research scaffolding, hypothesis brainstorming, and interview guide drafting under strict human review.

lessons.lesson_title: Double Diamond Framework, Product Thinking & Brief Deconstruction
lessons.what_is_taught: The commercial purpose of UX design: UI vs UX, interaction architecture vs visual styling, and the end-to-end product design lifecycle. Deconstructing client briefs using the Double Diamond model (Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver), balancing business needs against user desirability, and defining UX deliverables across product teams.
subtopics: UI vs UX: defining user experience, interaction architecture, and visual aesthetics
The digital product design lifecycle from initial discovery to commercial delivery
The Double Diamond model: Discover (Divergent), Define (Convergent), Develop (Divergent), Deliver (Convergent)
Human-centered design (HCD) principles and aligning business metrics with user needs
Product discovery fundamentals: assessing technical feasibility, business viability, and user desirability
Industry UX design roles: UX Researcher, Product Designer, UI Designer, and Design Systems Specialist
Anatomy of commercial UX deliverables: discovery decks, user flows, wireframes, and prototypes
lessons.why_it_matters: Jumping directly into visual interface design without problem validation leads to building products that look good but fail in the market. Problem framing ensures teams solve the right problems before solving them right.
lessons.what_learner_does: Analyze an ambiguous commercial FinTech/HealthTech brief, separate business goals from user needs, and map out a Double Diamond product discovery roadmap.
lessons.expected_outcome: A documented Product Discovery Canvas identifying core assumptions, market context, and primary research questions.
lessons.example: Reframing a client request from 'Build a flashy mobile savings app' to 'Reduce financial anxiety for young professionals through automated micro-investing and transparent fee structures.'

lessons.lesson_title: Qualitative User Research, Discussion Guides & Interview Execution
lessons.what_is_taught: Formulating research objectives, qualitative vs quantitative methodologies, and primary vs secondary market research. Authoring unbiased qualitative interview discussion guides, designing recruitment screeners in Google Forms, participant consent, and executing ethical 1-on-1 user interviews.
subtopics: Formulating actionable research objectives and establishing testable UX hypotheses
Qualitative vs quantitative methodologies: when to conduct interviews vs deploy surveys
Primary vs secondary market research and competitive heuristic analysis
Authoring unbiased user interview discussion guides with open-ended inquiry prompts
Designing recruitment screeners in Google Forms with qualifying filters and demographic targets
User recruitment protocols, informed participant consent, and ethical data privacy handling
Observational research and contextual inquiry concepts in real-world user environments
Identifying cognitive research bias: confirmation bias, framing effects, and leading questions
lessons.why_it_matters: Leading questions and biased interviews produce distorted data that misguide product development. Professional qualitative protocols reveal authentic user mental models and underlying emotional drivers.
lessons.what_learner_does: Author an objective 15-question user interview discussion guide, design a Google Forms recruitment screener, and conduct a supervised mock interview simulation.
lessons.expected_outcome: An approved interview discussion guide, screener survey link, and a raw interview transcript capturing verbatim user responses.
lessons.example: Replacing the leading question 'Do you find our current checkout page easy to use?' with the neutral, behavioral question 'Walk me through the last time you completed a purchase online—what worked smoothly, and where did you pause?'

lessons.lesson_title: Research Synthesis, Affinity Mapping & Insight Clustering in FigJam
lessons.what_is_taught: Processing raw interview notes and qualitative data in FigJam. Conducting affinity mapping, clustering data into inductive thematic categories, extracting behavioral patterns, and identifying authentic user pain points. Using AI (ChatGPT/Claude) for research summarization while strictly auditing outputs and enforcing authentic research integrity.

Collaborative affinity mapping mechanics in FigJam using tagged digital sticky notes

Distinguishing empirical evidence from designer assumptions and subjective stakeholder opinions
Identifying behavioral patterns, recurring friction points, and unmet user needs
Using ChatGPT for research synthesis: automated note summarization and theme extraction
Human auditing of AI synthesis: verifying AI suggestions against verbatim interview quotes
Ethical research boundaries: strictly prohibiting fabricated participant responses or synthetic interviews
lessons.why_it_matters: Raw interview transcripts are overwhelming and unmanageable. Affinity mapping systematically condenses dozens of qualitative data points into clear, actionable themes that guide interface architecture.
lessons.what_learner_does: Import 3 user interview transcripts into FigJam, extract 40+ raw observation notes on digital stickies, cluster them into 5 thematic insight pillars, and label key friction patterns.

lessons.lesson_title: Validated Personas, Empathy Maps & Customer Journey Mapping
lessons.what_is_taught: Translating synthesized insights into 4-quadrant Empathy Maps, validated user personas, and Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) statements. Data-driven personas vs fictional proto-personas: anchoring user archetypes in empirical evidence
The Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD) framework: 'When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [expected outcome]'

lessons.what_learner_does: Construct a 6-screen mid-fidelity wireframe set in Figma for a core user flow, featuring realistic UX microcopy, skeleton loading states, and an empty state.

modules.hands_on_practice: Create a complete information architecture, user flow diagram, and 6 mid-fidelity wireframe screens in Figma for a mobile app flow with state variations.

lessons.lesson_title: Figma Interface Architecture, Frames & Vector Mechanics
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating the Figma workspace: files, pages, sections, frames, layers, clipping masks, and vector networks. Frames vs Groups vs Sections: why frames are foundational to digital UI composition
Deep dive into Figma layers, z-index hierarchy, clipping masks, and blend modes
Vector networks engine: mastering the Pen tool, Bend tool, anchor points, handles, and path closing
Boolean operations: Union, Subtract, Intersect, and Exclude selection for custom vector shapes
Designing pixel-perfect 24x24px vector UI icons with a strict bounding box and 2px optical stroke weight
Figma styles management: creating, naming, updating, and detaching color and text styles

lessons.why_it_matters: Mastering Figma's canvas architecture and vector networks is the baseline technical requirement for any UI designer. Treating frames properly avoids broken layouts and unmanageable layer trees.

lessons.lesson_title: 8pt Spatial Cadence, Layout Grids & Gestalt Composition
lessons.what_is_taught: The 8pt spatial grid system and 4pt micro-grid architecture. Establishing layout grids across mobile (4-column), tablet (8-column), and desktop (12-column). Gestalt principles in digital UI (proximity, similarity, continuity), visual balance, optical centering, negative space discipline, and focal scanning vectors (F and Z patterns).
subtopics: The 8pt spatial grid system: mathematical logic, cognitive benefits, and developer alignment
The 4pt micro-grid: scaling typography, icons, and micro-padding elements with precision
Layout grids across breakpoints: 4-column mobile grids (16px margins), 8-column tablet, 12-column desktop (24px gutters)
Applying Gestalt principles to UI composition: proximity for card grouping, similarity for clickable elements, continuity for lists
Visual balance: symmetrical vs asymmetrical weighting, optical center vs geometric center
Negative space (white space) as an intentional layout element to reduce cognitive friction and highlight primary actions
Focal hierarchy: guiding user attention using scale contrast, tonal weight, and reading scanning vectors (F and Z patterns)
lessons.why_it_matters: Arbitrary spacing (e.g. 7px, 13px, 22px) makes interfaces look sloppy and amateurish while infuriating developers. An 8pt spatial grid ensures visual rhythm, harmony, and effortless code translation.
lessons.what_learner_does: Take an unaligned, cluttered mobile screen and refactor it onto a strict 4-column 8pt spatial grid, enforcing consistent 8px/16px/24px/32px spacing intervals throughout.
lessons.expected_outcome: A refactored mobile UI screen demonstrating rigorous 8pt spatial cadence, clean alignment, and intentional negative space.
lessons.example: Aligning a product card's internal padding to 16px, image-to-title gap to 12px (4pt micro-step), title-to-description to 8px, and card-to-card margin to 16px.

lessons.lesson_title: UI Typography Systems, Modular Scales & Text Hierarchy
lessons.what_is_taught: Typography architecture for user interfaces: selecting workhorse digital typefaces, constructing modular scales (Major Third, Perfect Fourth), establishing 7-level typographic hierarchies, optical line-height (leading), letter-spacing (tracking), line length constraints (measure), and mobile legibility standards.
subtopics: UI typography fundamentals: legibility vs readability, font classification, and selecting workhorse interface typefaces
Constructing modular typographic scales: Major Second (1.125), Minor Third (1.200), Major Third (1.250), Perfect Fourth (1.333)
Establishing a complete 7-level type hierarchy: Display, H1, H2, H3, Body-Large, Body-Regular, Caption/Overline
Optical line-height (leading) rules: tighter leading for display headlines (110–120%), relaxed leading for body text (140–160%)
Letter-spacing (tracking) adjustments: negative tracking for large titles, positive tracking for uppercase micro-labels
Measure and line length: constraining body text to optimal 45–75 characters per line for maximum reading comprehension
Mobile text hierarchy: optimizing touch screen legibility and minimum accessible font sizes (16px base body font)
Button and label typography: casing, weight, vertical alignment, and icon-to-text spatial pairing
lessons.why_it_matters: Interface design is 90% typography. A disciplined type scale immediately communicates content hierarchy, guides the user's reading eye, and elevates product polish to enterprise standards.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a complete typography style sheet in Figma using a Major Third modular scale, define responsive line-heights and letter-spacing, and typeset a content-heavy article screen.
lessons.expected_outcome: A published Figma typography style library and a typeset mobile screen demonstrating impeccable typographic hierarchy and readability.
lessons.example: Setting an 18px body font with 28px line-height (155%) for comfortable scanning, while setting a 32px headline with 38px line-height (118%) and -0.02em tracking.

lessons.lesson_title: Color Palettes, UI States & Visual Polish
lessons.what_is_taught: UI color theory, 60-30-10 distribution, semantic palettes (Primary, Secondary, Neutrals, Success, Warning, Error, Info), and accessible HSL tint curves. Engineering realistic multi-layer drop shadows and elevation depth. Designing core UI elements across all interaction states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error).
subtopics: Color theory in product interfaces: psychological impact, cultural associations, and brand alignment
The 60-30-10 visual distribution rule: 60% dominant neutral background, 30% structural secondary, 10% high-impact accent
Architecting a functional UI palette: Primary brand, Secondary, Neutral grays (9 tints/shades), and Semantic states (Success, Warning, Error, Info)
Generating accessible color tints using HSL/HCL lightness curves rather than arbitrary opacity blending
Elevation and depth: crafting multi-layered realistic drop shadows with ambient diffusion and directional light
Core UI element design: buttons, input fields, dropdowns, navigation bars, cards, tabs, and modal sheets
UI state variations: default, hover, focused (keyboard focus ring), active/pressed, disabled, loading skeleton, and error
Visual UI review checklist: pixel alignment, contrast audit, spacing verification, and design critique preparation
lessons.why_it_matters: Interfaces that only design default states break down when real users hover, click, encounter input errors, or experience slow network loading. Designing state variations is the hallmark of a professional UI designer.
lessons.what_learner_does: Convert approved low-fidelity wireframes into 3 polished, high-fidelity mobile UI screens featuring buttons, inputs, and cards across all interaction states.
lessons.expected_outcome: Three high-fidelity mobile UI screens in Figma accompanied by an interactive UI state variation sheet and documented color/typography tokens.
lessons.example: Designing an input field that clearly displays Default (gray border), Focus (2px primary blue ring + floating label), Filled (dark text), Error (red border + helper text), and Disabled (muted gray surface).

lessons.lesson_title: Auto Layout v5 Architecture, Nested Frames & Fluid Reflow

Layout directions: Horizontal row, Vertical column, and Auto Layout Wrap for dynamic chip and tag clouds

Component sets and multi-dimensional variant matrices: combining Type, Size, State, and Theme
Component properties: Boolean properties (toggling icon visibility), Text properties (editing label strings), and Instance Swap properties (swapping icon glyphs)
Eliminating variant bloat: using component properties to reduce a 128-variant button set down to a clean 16-variant matrix
Stateful components: engineering Default, Hover, Focused, Active/Pressed, Disabled, Loading, and Error states
Nesting atomic components into complex molecular components (e.g. assembling Button + Input + Label into a Search Bar)
Component library organization, naming conventions (Slash naming vs property naming), and publishing to team libraries

lessons.lesson_title: Figma Variables, Token Hierarchy & Light/Dark Theming

Token hierarchy: Global primitives (`blue-500: #3B82F6`) vs Semantic tokens (`surface-brand-primary: blue-500`) vs Component tokens (`button-bg: surface-brand-primary`)
Number variables: standardizing spatial padding scales (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32px) and border radii (4, 8, 16, 999px)
Variable modes: configuring Light Mode and Dark Mode variable collections
Switching variable modes across frames, sections, and entire page layouts with a single click
String variables: setting up multi-language text strings and localized mock content
Token management hygiene: organizing variable collections, aliases, and scoping variables to specific layer properties
lessons.why_it_matters: Hard-coded hex codes and arbitrary pixel values prevent product scaling. Design tokens and Figma Variables bridge design and frontend engineering, enabling instant light/dark theming and cross-platform token synchronization.
lessons.what_learner_does: Create a complete variable collection in Figma with primitive and semantic color tokens, bind them to a UI screen, and establish Light and Dark mode variations that toggle seamlessly.
lessons.expected_outcome: A multi-mode Figma variable collection and an interactive screen demonstration that toggles between Light and Dark themes with zero contrast errors.
lessons.example: Binding a card background to `surface-primary` which resolves to `#FFFFFF` in Light Mode and `#1E293B` in Dark Mode, while `text-primary` automatically shifts from `#0F172A` to `#F8FAFC`.

lessons.lesson_title: Responsive Breakpoint Engineering & Navigation Systems

Fluid layouts vs adaptive layouts: column reflow, stacking rules, and responsive image scaling
Responsive navigation architecture: adapting desktop horizontal navigation bars into mobile bottom tab bars and slide-out drawers
Honest Figma resizing behavior: understanding what Auto Layout can do natively (fluid stretching, wrapping) versus what requires dedicated breakpoint variants
Dispelling false claims: why standard Figma canvas does not automatically swap arbitrary component variants upon frame resize without dedicated breakpoint plugins or Framer

Interactive prototype transitions for responsive menus: prototyping hamburger menu slide-in, overlay backdrop, and close interactions
Exposure to Figma Sites: exploring Figma's evolving native web publishing and breakpoint-aware variant capabilities

lessons.lesson_title: WCAG 2.2 Digital Accessibility Standards & In-Canvas Auditing

Using Stark and in-canvas scanners, color vision deficiency simulation (Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia), touch target minimums (48x48px Android, 44x44px iOS), visible keyboard focus rings, and form error accessibility.

WCAG 2.2 AA standards: contrast ratio requirements (minimum 4.5:1 for body copy, 3:1 for large text and UI components)
Using Stark and in-canvas plugins to perform automated color contrast scans and identify violations
Color vision deficiency testing: simulating Protanopia, Deuteranopia, Tritanopia, and Achromatopsia
Touch target ergonomics: enforcing minimum 48x48px tap targets on Android and 44x44px on iOS with adequate spacing
Keyboard navigation: designing prominent, accessible focus states and visible focus indicators for all interactive elements

Screen reader awareness: annotating heading levels (H1–H6), alternative text (alt text), and reading order

lessons.lesson_title: Usability Testing Protocols, Task Scenarios & Maze Configuration
lessons.what_is_taught: Usability testing methodology: formulating research hypotheses, moderated vs unmoderated testing, authoring unbiased task scenarios, and defining quantitative metrics (Task Success Rate, Time on Task, Misclick Rate, System Usability Scale). Moderated testing protocols: think-aloud protocol, non-leading facilitation, and observational inquiry

Connecting Figma prototypes to Maze: setting up missions, defining expected paths, and setting success screens
Quantitative metrics in usability: Task Completion Rate, Time on Task, Misclick Rate, and Path Bounce Rate
The System Usability Scale (SUS): administering the standard 10-item questionnaire and scoring benchmarks

lessons.expected_outcome: An active Maze usability testing study with verified prototype integration, clear scenario prompts, and automated tracking metrics.

Differentiating usability flaws from user preference feedback and cosmetic critiques

Synthesizing qualitative user commentary into prioritized remediation recommendations
Authoring an executive Usability Test Report documenting methodology, key metrics, and evidence
Executing design iteration rounds: modifying layout, microcopy, and affordances based on empirical data

subtopics: What hiring managers look for: evaluating problem-solving logic, collaboration, and craft maturity over visual polish alone
Structuring the case study narrative: Problem, Role, Timeline, Discovery, IA, Wireframes, Testing, Final UI, and Impact
The STAR methodology in design documentation: framing concrete commercial situations and measurable results
Visual documentation hygiene: high-resolution screen mockups, animated prototype GIFs, and comparative before/after sliders
Highlighting design trade-offs: documenting what was intentionally discarded or deprioritized and explaining why
Curating the 3 canonical case studies: Consumer Mobile App (M01–03), Enterprise B2B SaaS (M04–06), and Live Marketing Website (M07)
Writing concise, compelling case study headlines and executive takeaway summaries for busy recruiters
lessons.why_it_matters: Hiring managers spend an average of 45 seconds reviewing a design portfolio. A disorganized gallery of final screenshots fails instantly; an articulate case study that proves research, iteration, and business impact wins interviews.
lessons.what_learner_does: Author an exhaustive, publication-ready case study for their primary capstone project, structuring problem framing, research evidence, iteration loops, usability testing metrics, and final Figma/Framer visuals.
lessons.expected_outcome: A complete, high-impact UX Case Study documented in Notion/Figma and ready for portfolio web publication.
lessons.example: Structuring a case study opening: 'Redesigning the onboarding experience for a preventative HealthTech app: How qualitative discovery and 3 usability iterations reduced 7-day drop-off by 24%.'

subtopics: Personal branding for product designers: crafting a clear value proposition and positioning statement
Information architecture of a designer portfolio: Home, Featured Projects, About Me, Resume, and Contact
Developing the portfolio in Framer: utilizing responsive Stacks, custom typography scales, and dark/light accents
Framer CMS for case studies: building dynamic project detail pages to showcase case study imagery and text
Embedding live interactive prototypes: configuring responsive iframe embeds for Figma prototypes and Loom video recordings
Interactive micro-interactions: adding subtle page transitions, hover states on project cards, and sticky contact anchors
Cross-device mobile QA, SEO meta tag validation, and publishing to a live `.framer.media` or custom domain
lessons.why_it_matters: A live Framer portfolio website immediately proves to employers that the designer can build and publish real digital products, setting them apart from 90% of applicants who only submit static PDF slides or Behance links.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build and publish a responsive, personal product design portfolio website in Framer showcasing 3 distinct case studies, embedded interactive prototypes, an about section, and a working contact form.
lessons.expected_outcome: A live, published personal portfolio website on `.framer.media` featuring responsive layouts, dynamic CMS case studies, and flawless navigation.

lessons.lesson_title: 1-Page ATS Resume Engineering, LinkedIn & Inbound Positioning
lessons.what_is_taught: Authoring an ATS-compliant, 1-page product designer resume. Structuring bullet points around quantifiable business achievements (Google X-Y-Z formula: Accomplished [X], as measured by [Y], by doing [Z]). Optimizing LinkedIn and Behance profiles for inbound recruiter search algorithms. Crafting tailored outreach messages to design leads and navigating recruiter screening calls.
subtopics: Applicant Tracking System (ATS) realities: standard typography, clean single-column layout, and eliminating multi-column visual clutter
Action-oriented resume writing: utilizing strong action verbs and quantifying project outcomes (conversion, speed, retention)
Highlighting core technical competencies: Figma Design Systems, Auto Layout v5, Framer Web Production, Maze Usability Testing, and AI Workflows
LinkedIn profile optimization: crafting search-optimized headlines, featured project carousels, and skill endorsements
Curating Behance and Dribbble showcases: formatting 1920x1080px presentation boards for visual design discoverability
Cold outreach strategy: crafting targeted, professional direct messages to design managers and recruitment partners
Preparing for recruiter screening calls: elevator pitch, salary expectations, and articulate career narrative
lessons.why_it_matters: Beautiful design files will never be seen if your resume is rejected by automated ATS screening filters. A clean, metrics-driven resume paired with an optimized LinkedIn profile ensures you consistently secure initial recruiter interviews.
lessons.what_learner_does: Typeset a 1-page ATS-compliant product designer resume in Figma/Word, optimize their LinkedIn headline and featured projects, and author a customized recruiter outreach message.
lessons.expected_outcome: A verified 1-page ATS-friendly PDF resume and an optimized, fully populated professional LinkedIn presence.
lessons.example: Transforming a weak resume bullet 'Designed mobile screens in Figma' into a powerful accomplishment: 'Architected a 10-component responsive UI kit in Figma with Auto Layout v5, cutting design-to-development handoff turnaround by 35%.'

lessons.lesson_title: Capstone Viva Voce Defense, Technical Interview Coaching & Graduation

Whiteboard design challenge strategies and technical critique resilience.

Formal Nova Skills Capstone Viva Voce defense evaluation and graduation certification
lessons.why_it_matters: In senior design hiring, interviews test how well a designer thinks, communicates, and defends trade-offs under scrutiny. Delivering an articulate viva voce defense proves graduates possess professional maturity and executive communication skills.
lessons.what_learner_does: Deliver a formal 15-minute live portfolio presentation walking through an end-to-end capstone project before faculty evaluators, defending design decisions and answering technical cross-examination questions.
lessons.expected_outcome: Successful oral viva voce defense of the 20-point Integrated Capstone and formal certification as a Certified UI/UX Design Professional.
lessons.example: Confidently explaining to an evaluator: 'We initially tested a floating bottom bar, but 4 out of 5 Maze participants missed the primary action due to banner blindness; we pivoted to a sticky card header which immediately restored task completion to 92%.'
